rationale: dual_domain_bilateral_n2i-claude-agentic: warm_start=True, pretrain_epochs=3, train_n=200, n_iter=300, val_n=16, batch_size=1, grad_clip=1.0, lr=0.005, proj_n_bf=1, img_n_bf=1, img_sr=0.0005, outer_wall_s=1500, seed=42, rationale=iter-3, ONE-KNOB change vs iter-1 (the BEST base: PSNR 38.17 dB, SSIM 0.9720). Knob: image-domain BF range sigma img_sr 0.02 -> 0.0005. EVERYTHING else identical to iter-1 (warm_start=True, pretrain_epochs=3, train_n=200, n_iter=300, val_n=16, grad_clip=1.0, lr=5e-3, proj_n_bf=img_n_bf=1, 6 trainable BF params, seed=42, proj sigmas back at Wagner-abdomen solver defaults). NUMBERS / WHY NOT iter-2's base: iter-2 tuned the PROJECTION-domain sigmas (proj_sx=0.01/proj_sy=0.3/proj_sr=0.0005) and PSNR went DOWN 38.17->37.90 dB (SSIM 0.9720->0.9680, RMSE up). So the proj-domain BF is NOT the over-smoother to fix here; reverting proj sigmas to iter-1 defaults and keeping iter-1 as the base. FAILURE MODE: hr=0, recon below the 39.68 dB LD-FBP baseline because the 6-param BF degrades an already-decent 128-view FBP. The design doc (solver_dual_ddomain_bilateral_n2i.md Weaknesses) pinpoints the IMAGE-domain BF as the over-smoother on breast-CT: 'Image-domain sigma_x grew 0.5->1.08 in 2 epochs on breast-CT iter-1 - saturating the kernel'; and the doc's own rule 'sigma_r << data range preserves edges; sigma_r >> data range degenerates to a Gaussian'. The CONFIG default img_sr=0.02 is too loose for the breast mu-range, so the image-domain BF degenerates toward a plain Gaussian that smooths ACROSS fibroglandular edges. HYPOTHESIS: tightening img_sr to 0.0005 (<< breast attenuation range) makes the image-domain BF edge-preserving instead of a Gaussian blur, so it stops smearing fibroglandular detail in the FBP and recovers PSNR toward (ideally above) the 39.68 dB LD-FBP baseline, lifting hr off 0. This mirrors the tight range-sigma logic the doc recommends for proj_sr, applied to the image domain where the over-smoothing actually lives. WALL: identical step budget to iter-1/2 (warm <=3x200=600 + per-image 16x300=4800), which completed in 241 s / 261 s - far under the 1800 s sbatch wall; outer_wall_s=1500 internal guard unchanged.
